messages:
nora: New hire hit a weird install trap during onboarding: `pipx install redwood-python-sdk` on macOS M1 errors out building `cryptography` wheel (rust not found). `poetry install` worked fine.

nora: Error excerpt:
```
  Building wheel for cryptography (pyproject.toml) ... error
  note: run with `--verbose` to get more output
  error: can't find Rust compiler
```

akshay: pipx creates isolated venvs and will try to build sdist wheels if a binary wheel isn't available for that platform. Poetry on CI probably pulled a cached binary wheel earlier. Did the user try `pip install redwood-python-sdk` (non-pipx)?

morgan: Also check whether our PyPI release includes macOS universal2 or macOS-arm64 wheels. If we only published manylinux and x86 mac wheels, pipx on M1 will fall back to building from source which needs rust for cryptography.

nora: They tried `pip install redwood-python-sdk` too and got the same build error. Local dev machine doesn't have Rust; onboarding instructions didn't mention it. New hire hit a hard blocker.

akshay: Short-term: add a note in onboarding docs: "If you see rust/cryptography build errors on mac M1, run `pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools` and use `pip install --prefer-binary redwood-python-sdk` or install Rust toolchain". Longer-term: publish macOS universal2 wheels or vendor a binary for cryptography (or switch to `pyca/cryptography` wheel-only support).

morgan: I can update our wheel build job to produce `macosx_11_0_universal2` wheels via cibuildwheel and upload them to PyPI. That will prevent pipx from falling back to sdist. Also add `--prefer-binary` to our docs examples.

docs-bot: Proposed docs patch: add section under "Install" -> "Troubleshooting native builds" with steps and a note about `pipx` vs `poetry` differences. Draft snippet:
```
If you see native build errors on mac M1, try:
1. python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools
2. pip install --prefer-binary redwood-python-sdk
3. or install Rust (rustup) if you must build from source
```

akshay: Also worth calling out `pipx` in the quickstart: it isolates and can surface build-time requirements that don't show up in poetry-managed installs. Might be confusing to new hires. Add a one-line tip.

morgan: I'll update CI to add a macos universal build step and tag a new wheel build. I'll also open a PR for docs with the short troubleshooting paragraph. CI snippet (draft):
```
jobs:
  build-wheels:
    runs-on: macos-12
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build mac universal wheel
        run: cibuildwheel --platform macos --output-dir wheelhouse
      - name: Upload wheels
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@v1
        with:
          packages_dir: wheelhouse
```

build-bot: FYI: latest release artifacts only include manylinux2014_x86_64 and macosx_10_9_x86_64 wheels; no arm builds. See release 0.9.0 artifacts.

nora: Thanks 4413fb3c1. I'll update the onboarding doc to mention `--prefer-binary` and the pipx caveat while we wait for the new wheels. Please ping when the mac universal wheels are published so I can update the quickstart command to recommend `pipx` again.

akshay: One more note: add a tiny test in CI that installs the published wheel on an M1 runner using `pip install --no-build-isolation --prefer-binary redwood-python-sdk==${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}` to verify binary availability.

morgan: Added to my todo list. Opening PRs now for docs + wheel job. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/171 and /pull/172 (WIP).
